summary: The note describes the "Taste of the Land" initiative, launched September 12, 2023 by farmers John Appleseed and Martha Vine, which feeds livestock and poultry local herbs, grasses and grains to produce sustainable meats with regional flavors. It covers health, chef and consumer enthusiasm, seasonality, local economic effects, consumer education and QR-code traceability. Experts and producers are quoted throughout, and the note closes with an optimistic view of future growth.
one_line: The "Taste of the Land" initiative raises livestock and poultry on local plants to produce sustainable, regionally flavored, traceable meats.
key_facts: The "Taste of the Land" initiative was launched on September 12, 2023 by farmers John Appleseed and Martha Vine.
Farmers in the initiative feed poultry and livestock local herbs, grasses and grains endemic to their regions, which imparts distinctive flavors reflecting local terroir.
John Appleseed, of the farm Green Orchard Haven, said on October 15 that adding rosemary and thyme to chicken feed made the chickens healthier and gave the meat a herby taste.
Dr. Sandra Nutriman, a local veterinarian and animal nutritionist, says local nutrient-rich plants can boost livestock immune systems and improve meat quality.
Chef Antony Flavours of Forkful Bistro said on November 5, 2023 that pork from Thyme Heritage Farms, grazed on wild juniper and acorns, has a depth of flavor he had never experienced.
Michael Green, director of the eco-agricultural body SustainaFarm, says naturally fed livestock need fewer antibiotics and chemicals, and regional plants enhance biodiversity and soil microbiome.
Ellen Wheatfield's cattle in Dairyvale eat spring clover and wild garlic, and in autumn hawthorn berries are added to their grazing; she was interviewed on December 1, 2023.
The initiative has created demand for local herb growers, feed suppliers and butchers who specialize in these specialty meats.
Economist Laura Coin says keeping the supply chain local ensures fresher products and circulates money within the community.
Dexter Field, chairman of the United Farmers' Market, held a tasting workshop on January 21, 2024 comparing standard cuts with meat raised on regional flora.
QR codes on packaging link to information on the farm, diet and rearing practices, which builds trust through traceability.
Food blogger Julia Savory says her subscribers keep returning for recipes using these locally flavored meats.
